items.subject: Mark Cuban on Why AI Could Turn Solo Founders Into Trillionaires
items.body:
Mark Cuban thinks AI could transform healthcare, but it won’t fix opaque prices and broken incentives on its own. His starting point for employers: run every benefits contract through AI and ask where you’re getting ripped off.
Mark joins a16z General Partner Julie Yoo and Erik Torenberg to discuss what he’s learned building Cost Plus Drugs, why trust is its core product, and how greater transparency could put pressure on healthcare costs.
They also explore where AI can help, what personalized medicine could look like, how the role of doctors may change, and why Mark believes founders should use AI to learn, not as an excuse to stop thinking.

items.subject: What Makes a Consumer AI Product Stick? | Josh Elman
items.body:
a16z Partner Josh Elman joins Ollie Forsyth on New Economies to discuss the next wave of consumer AI and what separates a product people try once from one that becomes part of their everyday lives.
Josh argues that getting attention has actually become easier, but getting consumers to stick is harder than ever. He explains what he looks for in consumer products, why the best ones start with a narrow wedge and earn the right to do more, and why trust becomes increasingly important as AI agents gain access to more of our personal lives.
They also explore personal AI agents, the future of shopping and entertainment, why we haven’t seen another major social network emerge, and how AI could make technology more social rather than less, including agents that help people spend more time together in the real world.
This conversation originally appeared on the New Economies podcast.

items.subject: Inside Cursor: The Anatomy of a Generational Startup
items.body:
a16z General Partners Martin Casado, Sarah Wang, and Matt Bornstein unpack the story of Cursor: how a small, product-obsessed team entered one of the most competitive markets in technology, took on incumbents with seemingly unbeatable advantages, and repeatedly made decisions that ran against conventional startup wisdom.
They revisit the early bet that the interface between humans and AI would matter more than building a coding-specific foundation model, why Cursor built its own product rather than a VS Code plugin, and how the founders' ability to say "no" became one of the company's defining strengths. They also discuss Cursor's rapid evolution from IDE to agent and model platform, and why the team was willing to cannibalize its own products as AI capabilities improved.
The conversation gets into what founders can learn from Cursor's approach to competition, hiring, enterprise sales, M&A, and company culture, including why the team remained unfazed by competitors from Microsoft to Anthropic and how its obsessive focus on product ultimately extended into every part of building the company.

items.subject: Stripe’s AI Strategy: Build More, Not Less
items.body:
a16z General Partner David George is joined by Will Gaybrick, President of Product & Business at Stripe, to discuss how AI is changing the way Stripe builds products, organizes teams, and thinks about the future of internet commerce. Stripe has evolved from a payments company into a multi-product financial infrastructure platform, while a new generation of AI companies is growing and monetizing faster than previous software cohorts.
Will explains why Stripe sees AI productivity as an opportunity to build more rather than simply cut costs, including how its internal coding agents now generate thousands of pull requests each week. They discuss creating founder-like agency inside large companies, building smaller and flatter teams, and why Stripe believes dramatically more software will be created as the cost of building continues to fall.
They also look ahead to agentic commerce, why checkout pages could disappear, the potential return of micropayments, stablecoins as infrastructure for a global economy, and a future where AI agents increasingly buy software and services from other machines.

items.subject: The Self-Improving Company | Kavak's AI Playbook
items.body:
Angela Strange and Gabriel Vasquez are joined by Alejandro Maza Ayala, Chief Product & AI Officer at Kavak, to unpack how the Latin American used-car marketplace rebuilt itself around AI agents, with 96% of customer interactions and 95% of transactions now handled by agents.
Alejandro explains why Kavak decided that simply giving employees AI tools wasn't enough, and instead redesigned the company's systems, teams, and customer experience around agents. They discuss why Kavak spends as much engineering effort on evals as it does building agents, how its AI sellers outperform its human teams, and an experiment where an AI "CEO" increased profits in one city by 50% in its first month.
The conversation also explores what happens to organizational structure when agents do most of the work, why Kavak trains everyone from executives to mechanics to build with AI, and Alejandro's argument that companies looking for incremental AI adoption may be missing the larger opportunity: redesigning the organization itself.

**Key Developments:**

* **AI-powered design canvas**: Agentic Canvas, a free visual design tool, was launched on Product Hunt, allowing users to work with AI in a collaborative and intuitive way.
* **AI-powered identity and inboxes**: Puffin, a new product, was launched on Product Hunt, enabling AI agents to manage identities and inboxes.
* **AI-powered office software**: OffiAI, a new product, was launched on Product Hunt, which is essentially an office software with AI capabilities.
* **AI-powered UI components**: UI SDK, a new product, was launched on Product Hunt, providing AI agents with building blocks to create user interfaces.
* **AI-powered CAD design**: LexiCAD, a new product, was launched on Product Hunt, allowing users to describe parts in plain language to get a CAD design.
* **AI-powered monitoring**: AgentWatch, a new product, was launched on Product Hunt, enabling users to monitor AI shopping agent sales and visibility on Shopify.

**Trend:**

* **Increased focus on AI-powered productivity tools**: The recent launches on Product Hunt suggest a growing trend towards AI-powered productivity tools, which aim to make work more efficient and collaborative. These tools often involve AI agents that can assist with tasks, provide design suggestions, and even manage identities and inboxes. This trend is likely to continue as AI technology advances and more businesses seek to automate and streamline their operations.
